summary: A real-time game steered by discrete commands (Light Cycles) was shown two snapshots behind the authority: four ticks at 15 snapshots a second, longer than a three-tick step. A turn chosen from the arena on screen always took effect on the step after the next one, so no rider ever turned on its next step. Command-steered games now show the latest authoritative frame; games with held controls keep their playback buffer.
